side_a: CC 3.1.3.1 "The horizon is the row's own `valid_until`" … "A row without `valid_until` is malformed on this family."
side_b: CC 2.1 "If set, consumer policy treats the attestation as stale after that point, independent of the row's own `expires_at`."
note: CC 3.1.3.1 requires `valid_until` on every `session:*` row and makes it the one staleness instant for every reader. CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.7 list only `session_id` and `claimed_at` as REQUIRED on `session:*` and give `valid_until` as OPTIONAL consumer policy on every row. A door built from the signed-object table admits a claim with no horizon, which a dead node then holds for ever; CC 3.1.3.1 is the home and the table lacks the row.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.1 "A row without `valid_until` is malformed on this family."
side_b: manifests/family_model.json session:{kind} body members session_id, claimed_at, community_id (each "presence": "required") and no other; lifecycle "expires": "expires_at honoured"
note: The body cell of `session:{kind}` lists three required members and not `valid_until`, and its lifecycle cell reads expiry from `expires_at`, where the text makes the signed `valid_until` the horizon. `manifests/reactions.json` has it right (expiry required, member `valid_until`, at most `session_claim_max_secs` from `claimed_at`), so the data disagrees with itself and only the family-model cells are to fix.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.3 "**(5) Freshness is the row's.** The 72-hour window below is the claim's `expires_at`; no second TTL exists."
side_b: CC 3.1.3.3 "A report is **live for 72 hours** from its instant" … "A report older than 72 hours reads as *unknown*"
note: Rule (5) makes the lapse the row's signed `expires_at`; the Freshness paragraph (and CC 5.3.2.1) makes it 72 hours from the report's instant. No text requires `expires_at` on `custody:ack` (CC 2.6.1.7 requires it only on the two census shares, CC 2.1 only on a membership proposal) or fixes it at instant plus 72 h. A report minted without it, or with a longer one, counts as a holder for ever or for longer under rule (5) and for three days under the Freshness paragraph. `manifests/reactions.json` decides it (expiry required, `expires_at` equal to `asserted_at` plus `custody_report_ttl_secs`); the text and the signed-object table do not say so. Minor because a careful reader takes rule (5) to mean the member is set to the instant plus 72 hours; the two differ only for a report minted without the member or with another value, which nothing in the text refuses. Same family of fault as C356.

side_b: manifests/family_model.json custody:{kind} body "custody_state here|none, evidence_refs exactly one blob digest"

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "dimension prefix on `scores`: `key_grant:{axis}:v1` ([CC 3.3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)), or the `consent:scope:*` family"
side_b: CC 3.3.1 "A `consent:scope:{kind}` dimension row, if anyone emits one, is **descriptive** — no fold reads it and it confers nothing"
note: The triad's wire discriminator for a grant (and the `grant` scope row of CC 4.4.3.4.3, "a `consent:scope:*` grant") names the dimension family that CC 3.3.1 says confers nothing; the grant is the `scope` member of `consent:state:granted`. Same fault as C188 (CC 3.4.5), in three more places (CC 4.5.1.1 also calls `consent:scope:{…}` a permitted-use gate); CC 3.3.1 decides.

side_a: CC 2.4 "**membership events** (`membership:widening:v1` / `removal:v1` / `resignation:v1`, cosigned, beside the single-signer proposal, acceptance and decline)"
side_b: CC 3.1.3.2 "a widening or removal is cosigned under the group's `consensus_protocol`, a resignation is signed by the leaving member"
note: CC 2.4 lists the resignation among the cosigned events, and the roster-fold comment of `resolve_community` and `resolve_family` says "revocations, widenings, resignations, each admitted per CURRENT consensus_protocol". CC 3.1.3.2 and CC 3.3.4 make it the leaver's own single-signer row, and the family model agrees (cosign none on resignation). A door built from CC 2.4 or the fold comment holds a member in the group until a quorum signs. The rest of the document supports the leaver alone (exit is the member's own).

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3.1 "That core is eight members present in every `:v1` half." … "Additional REQUIRED members are a `:v2` bump, never a silent `:v1` addition."
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "a row with no mirror is refused `envelope_member_missing`"
note: The partnership signing set is a flat object whose eight members put `attestation_type` and `attesting_key_id` at the top level, with no `row` mirror, no `cohort_scope`, no `score` and no `confidence`. CC 2.6.1.7 requires the mirror (closed seven, `cohort_scope` among them) and `score` and `confidence` on every `scores` row. Bytes signed to the eight-member contract are refused at the CC 2.6.1.7 door, and bytes that pass the door carry REQUIRED members the contract calls a `:v2` bump. The login `delegates_to` and occurrence shapes of the same section are flat in the same way. CC 2.6.1.7 is generated from data with vectors, so the section is the stale side.

In a code block; CC 3.3.2 is the home.

note: Still present. `source_count` is REQUIRED on `ballot:tally:{poll_id}:v1` under a note that refuses fewer than ten; the `ballot:tally` registry row lists four refusals and no below-k one, and CC 6.1.9 gives a tally the dominance gate only. side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "H(node_secret ‖ period): the per-period token a contributor later checks for inclusion; never a node id."
note: The table reads this as no conflict because "the return's token is one per owner per period". The text derives the token from `node_secret`, and the duplicate rule keys on `(return_token, share_index)`, so an owner of eight nodes sends eight tokens and nothing stated at the door folds them to one source. `constants.tsv` (census_k_floor) says "one accepted return per owner per period". The ground of the no-conflict reading is still not in CC 6.1.9, CC 3.1.3 or CC 2.6.1.7.

side_b: manifests/governance_policy.json base_law "base(N) = N if N <= k else max(min, k + (N - k) // tail); rows with base=standing use N"
note: Still present. The decider takes its base from roster size alone (k 12, tail 30, min 3); the text takes it above `k` from `census:expected_active:v1` under the ratchet, with a floor of the larger of rooted-active members and half the last stable count. Both are marked provisional and they are different functions: a roster of 100 gives 14 in the data whatever the census says.

side_b: manifests/family_model.json census:expected_active fold "combine=max(count(owner),(prev*9+9) div 10,floor)"
note: Still present, in a changed form: the earlier freeze test is gone from the fold cell and nothing replaced it. The cell now carries the tenth-per-period ratchet and the floor and no freeze or release. On a fall from 30 to 10 the text holds the base at 30 until a period returns 20; the fold gives 27, then 25. (C347, the window applied twice, is fixed: the cell reads `over=active/owner`.)

side_b: CC 6.1.9 "The floor is the standing roster at or below the size `k` of the base law in the [CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13) policy table."
note: One section now uses `k` for two numbers: the suppression floor of ten sources, and the roster size (12 in the data) up to which the base is the standing roster. The second came in with the repair of C353. A reader who carries k = 10 into the floor sentence gets a different base for rooms of 11 and 12.

side_b: manifests/family_model.json census:share:{class} fold "key=period,token; pick=once(census_share_duplicate_token)"
note: The text's duplicate key is (token, share index, seat, period); the fold cell's is (period, token). Read as written the fold refuses the second of a return's two shares wherever both are held, which is the author's own node. The same holds for `census:member:share` (`ballot_share_duplicate_token`).

side_b: CC 6.1.9 "A composite is a histogram per field per cell. A reader computes the median bucket and the trimmed statistics from it" … "The published rows carry exact field sums."
note: Part 1 has the composite publish a median; the home has it publish the whole histogram with exact sums, the median being the reader's computation. What an observer of a published cell learns differs (a distribution, not one bucket). CC 6.1.9 and CC 2.6.1.7 (`mass_total`, summed histograms) are the supported side; the Part 1 row is loose wording of the same kind C156 settled for rounding.

side_b: CC 4.5.13 "A default is otherwise admissible only for a choice that narrows or keeps things as they are" … "**Relay offering is the stated exception:**"
note: Still present. Announcing writes the owner-binding at federation scope, a widening, and starts on; CC 5.4.6 refuses that binding for an owner who resolves to the `minor` band, which is every owner with no assurance on record. Within CC 4.5.13 the default rule also names one exception (relay offering) while announcing is a second.

side_b: manifests/transitions.json membership:{stage} attest "confirm": {"value": true, "source": "derived", "when": "always"}
note: Leaving a room is an attest of `membership:resignation`, and a decline is an attest too. The transition row splits roles and policy by stage and does not split `widens` or `confirm`, so every stage is confirmed, the two narrowing ones included. `ui_primitives.json` law L6 reads the confirm cell from this manifest and says "leaving a membership is never slowed by a confirm". The other 455 confirm cells follow the rule (checked mechanically: confirm iff widens or no way back).

side_b: manifests/choice_item.cddl "a row of constitution/governance_policy.tsv by family (self_choice for a first-run or consent item)"
note: The policy table has sixteen rows and none is `self_choice`, and none is one voice of one with no window: the two self rows are `self_roster_add` and `self_roster_evict`, two-path with a window of 86 400 s. `transitions.json` calls the one-voice policy `selfAct` with no row. A validator that checks an item's `policy` against the table refuses every first-run and consent item.

side_b: manifests/choice_item.cddl write "scope: \"self\" / \"family\" / \"community\" / \"affiliations\" / \"federation\""
note: An option's `writes` names the scope of the row it would sign from five values, and the item's `circle` from the same five; the envelope's `cohort_scope` has seven. An item whose row is placed at `species` or `biosphere` cannot be written in the schema, so the queue cannot offer a transition the door admits ("the queue never offers what the door would refuse and the door never admits what the queue would not have offered").

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "The row is held by the author's node and this key's node and by no other" … "Also carried on consent:state rows."
side_b: CC 3.3.1 "Subject's stance on the target Contribution. Closed-set stance values; `revoked` overrides prior `granted`."
note: `for_key_id` is stated for a `consent:state` row only in the last sentence of the table's note, under a rule (two holders, every other node refuses `federation_addressed_not_recipient`) written for a census share. No section of Part 3 names the member on a consent row or says who holds such a row; CC 3.3.1 and CC 4.5.3 have a revocation reach every holder by its scope. A door built from the note makes a consent row carrying the member invisible to all but one node. The note needs its own sentence for the consent case, or the home needs the member.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is `u64` **big-endian** and monotonic per RNS Link (transit replay guard).
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is a per-`(link, stream)` counter both ends keep and is never carried in the frame
note: still present: one counter per link or one per (link, stream) gives different outer nonces and the hop fails to open; the nonce formula carries no stream id and the outer seal is per link, so per link is supported

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 is a 64-byte Ed25519 signature by the bound chunk key, appended to the inner unit after the inner ciphertext and inside the outer seal
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 the shipping form, which precedes the signature with an 8-byte publisher timestamp `source_ms` under the domain `ciris-edge:av-chunk-sig:v2`
note: still present: the laid-out trailer, the last-64-bytes relay step, the 148-byte budget and the known answers are the v1 form; the sentence says the shipping form is v2 with 8 more bytes; a v1 builder and a v2 builder refuse each other as av_chunk_trailer_invalid

side_a: CC 5.3.3.1 On epoch roll the DEK changes, so a reset counter lives in a different keyspace
side_b: CC 5.3.3.1 Substrate MUST reject a chunk-append whose `(stream_id, seq)` collides with an existing sealed chunk (the replay and forking guard).
note: CC 5.3.3.2.5 sets the nonce counter equal to the header chunk_seq. Read with the first side, chunk_seq restarts at each epoch (and only a restart makes the forced roll before 2^32 avoid a wrap); read with the second side and CC 5.3.3.3 (leaves in seq order, tree_size the chunk count of the whole stream) seq is unique across the stream and never restarts. The two builds derive different nonces from epoch two on, or one refuses the other's chunk 0 as a collision. Nothing states whether chunk_seq is per epoch or per stream; CC 3.3.13 (sequence_start, HLS sequence numbers) leans per stream

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 Every `accord:invoke:*` Contribution signs the canonical bytes below.
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 The signing input is JCS(attestation_envelope) and nothing else.
note: CC 4.2.1.1 has a consumer verify the holder signature over sha256 of the labelled newline-joined fields; CC 2.6.1.7 says a row signature covers JCS of the envelope and nothing else, and types no member that could carry a second signature. CC 5.3.3.6 and CC 5.3.3.3 state the two-layer reading for receipts and stream roots; no sentence states it for accord:invoke, accord:lifecycle (CC 4.2.1.3) or the CC 4.2.6 proposal and participation. A halt signed over one input does not verify under the other

side_a: CC 3.1.3 id = sha256(domain ‖ JCS(object)); a receiver re-derives the row and refuses any byte difference
side_b: manifests/signed_object.cddl uuid = tstr .regexp "[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}"
note: CC 3.1.3 gives the minted identity:occurrence_revocation row, and the cosign:signature row, an id that is a SHA-256; the table and CDDL type attestation_id as a 36-character UUID and the gate refuses an ill-typed member. How 32 digest bytes become the UUID is nowhere stated, and the receiver refuses any byte difference, so two mints of one object can refuse each other

side_a: CC 4.5.13: "It is on by default for servers and home nodes under the device policy of"
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "**Relay is offered by default on every owned node**, the shaped mesh standing on it."
note: CC 4.5.13 names servers and home nodes; CC 5.4.6 says every owned node, then gives the phone its own default (charging on an unmetered network). A careful reader reaches the device policy either way; cf. C143.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "and a node that activated the tier holds that identity alone (one identity per node, below)"
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "The tier's activation on a node is therefore the act that turns shaping on for that node's layer links"
note: Activating the tier means entering anonymous mode in the first sentence and becoming a relay in the second (item 4, which lets "the fleet default" govern the node's other links, where an anonymous node holds only shaped layer and rendezvous links). CC 5.4.3 "a node set to shaped-only or to the Anonymous Tier" refuses a row link past the bound: a default relay reading the second sense would refuse where the text means only an anonymous node.

side_a: CC 5.4.3: "Maintenance traffic (anti-entropy, replication, witness, repair) and ordinary rows are shaped."
side_b: CC 5.4.3: "Chat and files ride a shaped link only when one end of it is shaped-only."
note: Item 4 puts ordinary rows on the shaped link; the later paragraph sends an offering pair's chat over an unshaped link beside it. The table records it as no conflict on reading; reported for the overlap.

side_a: CC 3.1.4: "each period's row `supersedes` the previous one in the same lineage, and a row is purgeable after `valid_until`"
side_b: data family_model.json (rendezvous:route, lifecycle): "supersedes": "same_attester"
note: CC 3.1.4 and CC 5.4.6 item 6 sign each period's row with a fresh rendezvous key (attester = subject = the period's key), yet have it supersede the previous period's row. The data (and the CC 8.10 card: supersede by author) admit a supersede only from the same attester, as CC 2.4.1 defines the verb, so the next hour's row cannot supersede. Expiry at valid_until does the work in practice; the supersedes clause cannot be followed.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "**Yes — the accord holders, cosigned at the charter's M**; never a single holder, never the node itself"
side_b: data transitions.json (transport:canonical_rebind, supersede): "policy": "selfAct"
note: Partly still present. The attest row of the CC 8.10 card now reads cosigned accord_majority, but its supersede row still reads author, selfAct: one holder replacing a quorum re-bind alone. The text allows no single-holder act on the binding.

side_a: CC 3.3.5: "Subject withdraws; producer must initiate deletion within sla window"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "A producer has proven deletion **iff**, before the deadline, the row was **withdrawn, superseded, or hard-deleted**"
note: What is owed by the end of the window: deletion begun (CC 3.3.5) or deletion done (CC 3.3.1 D1, and CC 2.4.1.1 "deletes within it"). A producer that has only started at the deadline conforms to one and is in breach under the other. D1, the reaction data and CC 2.4.1.1 support done.

side_a: CC 4.5.2.2: "producer emits `consent:deletion_complete` OR substrate emits `hard_case:deletion_window_breach`"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "that emission is evidence **toward** D1 and never a substitute for it"
note: Still present in the CC 4.5.2.2 compliance row (the CC 4.4.3.5.2 pseudocode C304 named no longer reads "completion is None"). The row lets a completion attestation stand in place of the breach; D1 and manifests/reactions.json cancel the breach only on a withdrawal, supersession or purge of the row.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "A signer that committed to a deletion window deletes within it and keeps no copy"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "CC **declines** a distinct affirmative `deletion_proof` artifact: the three structural composers already leave an auditable, replay-checkable trace"
note: D1 counts a supersedes or a withdraws of the row as deletion proven, either of which can land while the bytes remain; CC 2.4.1.1 requires that no copy is kept. D1 is a proof rule and the other a duty, so a careful reader holds both, but a watcher built on D1 alone cannot see the duty kept.

side_a: CC 6.1.2.3: "→ `EjectHardDelete` **regardless of pin state** (the fastest descent, never tier-shed — CC 6.1.2)"
side_b: CC 6.1.5: "is admitted and recorded, and the descent it would force is refused with reason under that declared gate"
note: The verdict mapping (and CC 6.1.5.2 B6, CC 6.1.5.3 "Consent is supreme at every tier") force hard delete on any withdraws or revocation and name none of N5's gates (erasure_exempt or legal_hold; the signer's kept copy). N5 is the home. Same fault as C047, in the restatements of my share.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.8: "so a right-to-be-forgotten / N5 signal is **refused-with-reason** rather than honored"
side_b: CC 6.1.5: "is admitted and recorded, and the descent it would force is refused with reason under that declared gate"
note: CC 4.4.3.2.8 refuses the signal; CC 6.1.5 N5 and CC 4.4 (the withdrawal paragraph) admit and record the withdraws and refuse only the descent. An implementer reading 4.4.3.2.8 alone may refuse the row at the door, leaving it live to its audience. N5 and CC 4.4 agree with each other.

side_a: CC 4.5.3: "There is no node-local purge basis for erasure."
side_b: data family_model.json (trace:{form}:{version}, erasure_route): "dsar (trace corpus hard delete)"
note: Still present in the data (source code-v61): the model carries a node-local hard delete of the trace corpus on a subject request, where CC 4.5.3 sends a trace "the same way", by its signer's withdraws or a named party's, with the replicated tombstone. C228 settled the text side.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "a `slashing:*` verdict, a `quarantine:*` marker"
side_b: data family_model.json (quarantine:{state}, lifecycle): "withdraws_by": "{attester, subject}"
note: Still present in the data. The kept list now names the quarantine marker, so its subject may not withdraw it; the lifecycle cell (code-v61) still lets the subject withdraw. Every other kept-list family (capacity, detection, licensure, revocation, moderation, hard_case, slashing, takedown_notice) reads attester only.

side_a: CC 4.5.3: "serving resumes, the hard-delete sweep skips them, and the holder re-acknowledges `here`"
side_b: data reactions.json (takedown_notice:{basis}, on close of withhold): "act": "destroy_bytes"
note: Still present. All four windowed bases now have their clock (C376 is repaired), but each close-of-window reaction destroys the bytes with no unless for an admitted reversal, where the text has the sweep skip bytes whose notice was reversed inside the window.

side_a: CC 4.2: "it reaches exactly those holding a live trust edge to the accord when it is fired"
side_b: CC 4.2.1: "at the instant the halt becomes active at that node"
note: Reach is judged when the halt is fired (CC 4.2) or when each node's store admits the row and latches (CC 4.2.1, 4.2.1.1). A node that cuts its edge between the two is reached under one and not the other. CC 4.2 cites CC 4.2.1 for reach and a node cannot know the firing instant, so the latch reading stands; the CC 4.2 sentence is the older wording.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.3: "**It is a cosigned row by a strict majority of the standing roster** (`additional_scrubs[]`"
side_b: data family_model.json (accord:lifecycle:{kind}, cosign_rule): "value": "none"
note: The resumption and the confirmation are cosigned by a strict majority in CC 4.2.1.3, 4.2.1.1, 3.1.1 and 3.4.1, and CC 4.2.1.3 says "never a lone signature". The family model's cosign cell (read from the shipped store) says none, while its own count cell and the transition case (leaf=active: cosigned accord_majority) agree with the text. A reader of the cosign cell admits a one-holder resumption.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.3: "`accord:lifecycle:active` is the **only** sanctioned resumption after a `constitutional` halt"
side_b: data family_model.json (accord:invoke:constitutional:{halt_id}, lifecycle): "withdraws_by": "{attester, subject}"
note: The lifecycle cell (code-v61) lets the firing holder or a subject withdraw a halt row; the text ends a halt only by the fuse or a strict-majority resumption, and the verbs cell of the same row is attest only. Whether a withdrawn halt row clears a latch is stated nowhere; the text gives one holder no way to un-fire.

side_a: CC 4.5.4: "A `community` is admitted, and continues to federate, **only while ≥1 member holds the live `moderate` duty**"
side_b: CC 4.5.13: "So a community with no live holder of `moderate` **locks**: read-only to everyone, since nobody can moderate."
note: What a room without a moderator does: stops federating and is non-conformant (CC 4.5.4 gate 1 and rule 3, "MUST NOT federate / operate") or stays served read-only while its members' ballots travel and seat one (CC 4.5.4 rule 2, CC 4.5.13). An election cannot run in a room that has stopped federating. Rule 2 and CC 4.5.13 agree; "nobody may post, admit or act" likewise leaves the ballot and the acceptance row unstated as exceptions.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "Consequences — slashing verdicts, de-admission decisions by other nodes — remain [CC 4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md) WA-quorum or per-node acts"
side_b: data family_model.json (slashing:{outcome}, signer_rule): "who": "any_registered"
note: Every text statement puts a slashing verdict with an adjudicating body (CC 3.3.1 D3 and CC 3.3.5.1 "follows on WA quorum"; CC 2.4.1.1 calls it a duty-holder's record). The family model (code-v61) admits a slashing:{outcome} row from any registered key with no cosignature and no governance row; the home row in CC 3.1.9.2 names no signer. A store built from the data admits a lone key's verdict against staked standing.

side_a: CC 3.3.10.1: "via `slashing:*` ([CC 3.1.9.3](part_3_the_namespace.md))"
side_b: CC 3.3.5.1: "slashing:{outcome} (CC 3.1.9.2) against staked standing"
note: Two citations for the home of slashing. The slashing:{outcome} row sits in the CC 3.1.9.2 table; CC 3.1.9.3 is the consensus-mechanics table and holds no slashing row.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.3: "**`federation` for Commons and `public` content**. The substrate refuses a report whose scope is not its content's."
side_b: CC 5.2: "the only plaintext bodies are those of authorized infrastructure communities and public rooms, which"
note: CC 5.2 and CC 1.13.3.4 put an authorized infrastructure community's holding claims at federation scope with the public room's; CC 3.1.3.3 rule (1) names only Commons and public content for federation and refuses any other report whose scope is not its content's (`community`). A reader of rule (1) refuses the infrastructure community's federation-scope custody report that a reader of CC 5.2 emits. CC 4.4.3.2.1 (plaintext by the record) supports CC 5.2.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3: "has an allow list of only the cohorts it was set up to serve"
side_b: CC 3.3.7: "receives **no** `self` content beyond the two arms below, and **no** `family` content unless the list names it"
note: A server-class node whose grant carries no `cohorts` member: CC 6.1.5.3 gives it only the cohorts it was set up to serve; the class default of CC 3.3.7 (and the later sentence of CC 6.1.5.3) withholds only self and family, so every community and affiliation of its owner replicates onto it. The two give different holdings for the owner's other communities. Near C381 (which asks about agents), not the same point.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.1: "**Projection ceiling: `Cohort` at every commons tier, with no `authority` branch (normative — not a default).**"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json session:{kind} placement: "any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text forbids a session claim above the cohort (an attendance map of a person's devices); the model cell lets the signer place it in the commons, where the replication cell serves it to everyone. The cell is marked a gap; the text has the value.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.3: "the audience is the cell (for an agent, the steward's cohort and the WA it routes to), never a federation broadcast"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json deferral:request placement: "any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text bounds a deferral request to the deferring party's cell; the model cell admits it at commons placement with audience everyone, and the CC 8.10 card shows attest widening by scope. Text has the value; the data cell is a gap.

side_a: CC 3.1.4: "A federation-scope row whose attester and subject are one **rendezvous key**"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json rendezvous:route placement: "any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text fixes the route row at federation scope with reach everyone; the model cell leaves placement to the signer. A route placed narrower reaches no sender, so a careful reader resolves it the text's way.

side_a: CC 3.2: "there is no member-level listing, and a roster is never enumerable outside its cohort, a public room's included"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json membership:{stage} replication.audience note: "may_receive_group_plane (public group: everyone; private: members' nodes, live invitees, named member); proposal: addressee (invitee)"
note: CC 3.2 and the CC 5.2 audience table (public room: an outsider learns the listing, the holding claims and the content, "never the roster") keep a public room's membership rows inside its roster; the model cell serves a public group's membership rows to everyone, which makes the roster enumerable by any node.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "A node offers an `identity:occurrence:v1` row to a peer only when it would also relay the row's attester key to that peer"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json identity:occurrence replication.audience note: "key-plane reach (Plane::KeyRecord cells; the carrier: everyone)"
note: CC 5.4.6 withholds an occurrence whose attester's owner-binding is not announced, and holds an unannounced identity's occurrence with the owner's nodes and the contact alone; the model cell gives the family one audience, everyone. A kernel reading the cell serves an unannounced person's occurrence to strangers.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "**Yes — addressed:** a member of the room; reach is the named tally member only"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json census:member:share replication.audience: "cohort_plus_subjects(full) (refers-to: attested, subjects, for_key_id)"
note: Same fault as C383 on the sibling family: the text holds a member's community cell with its author and the one tally member it is addressed to; the model cell keeps the default audience (the whole cohort plus subjects) under an `addressed` placement.

side_a: CC 6.1.9: "is held by the author's node and the recipient's node and by no other"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json census:share:{class} replication.audience: "cohort_plus_subjects(full) (refers-to: attested, subjects, for_key_id)"
note: Still present: the census:share:{class} replication cell still carries the default audience, not the addressee.

side_b: data manifests/family_model.json moderation:{allegation_type} replication.audience: "cohort_plus_subjects(full) (refers-to: attested, subjects, for_key_id)"
note: Still present: the moderation cell still serves the full row to the subject; the text lets the record reach the person named as existence, kind, consequence and answerer only.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.1: "An observer learns that a group exists, roughly how big it is, and when its membership churns."
side_b: CC 2.1: "So `family_id` is consulted in-substrate and never on the wire to non-members."
note: Still present (resolution proposed, not applied): CC 1.13.3.1 concedes that an observer sees a family's existence, size and churn; CC 2.1 and the CC 5.2 table (an outsider learns nothing, "not even that the content exists", and nothing of the roster) deny it unless the observer is inside the cohort.

side_a: CC 6.1.1: "`cohort_scope: family | community` content MAY be witnessed **only at the opaque `content_id`/manifest-digest grain**"
side_b: CC 5.2: "the only attestations that refer to them are scoped to the cohort and never federate beyond it"
note: CC 6.1.1 does not state the audience of a wholeness witness whose leaves include family content, and WW-4 publishes a `leaf_count`; CC 5.2 lets no row that refers to family bytes leave the cohort. A careful reader places such a witness at the family's scope, which CC 6.1.1 should say.

side_a: CC 3.1.4: "each period's row `supersedes` the previous one in the same lineage"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json rendezvous:route supersede roles: "author"
note: CC 3.1.4 gives each period a fresh rendezvous key that is attester and subject of its row, so the row that supersedes last period's is signed by a different key; the transition (and the CC 2.4.1 gloss, "by the same attester") lets only the prior row's author supersede. A kernel run from the data refuses every period's successor. The supersedes link also ties one period's key to the next, which the fresh key was to prevent.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7: "a Goal is amended by `supersedes`, retired by `withdraws`, and disowned by `recants`"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json goal:{scale} verbs: ["attest", "replace", "withdraw"]
note: The text gives a Goal's declarer `recants`; the model's verb cell (source cc-table) and the transitions omit it, though the cell's own code reading records "+recant". A door built from the data refuses the recant the text admits. approach:{goal_id} carries recant; goal does not.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.3: "(`supersedes` to revise, `withdraws` to satisfy/close, `recants` if misstated)"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json need:{domain}:{kind} verbs: ["attest", "replace", "withdraw"]
note: Same fault as goal:{scale}: the text gives a need row `recants`, the verb cell and transitions have attest, supersede and withdraw only.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7: "its `supersedes`, `withdraws` and `recants` stand only when they too are cosigned under the same protocol"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json goal:{scale} supersede: roles "author", policy "selfAct"
note: For a Goal a group declared, the text requires the amendment, retirement and disowning to be cosigned under the group's protocol; the model has cosign_rule none and one-signer supersede and withdraw, so one member who signed first amends or retires the group's Goal alone. The same holds for approach, method and progress_measure rows a group declares.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "`census_composite_duplicate_period` (a second composite for the class and period, from any seat)"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json census:composite:{class}: verbs attest, withdraw, supersede; supersede roles "author"
note: The text allows one composite per class and period and refuses a second from any seat; the transitions and the CC 8.10 card give the signing seat a supersede (and a withdraw), which is a second composite for the same class and period. census:partial:{class} carries the same supersede against "one per (seat, class, period)".

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "**Yes — the accord holders, cosigned at the charter's M**; never a single holder, never the node itself"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json transport:canonical_rebind supersede: roles "author", policy "selfAct"
note: The attest transition now carries the cosigned accord policy (C369, C374 fixed there), but the supersede transition beside it is still one-signer: the holder who authored a re-bind replaces it alone, which is a re-bind by a single holder. The CC 8.10 card shows the same line.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: "A `family` Contribution that supersedes the current one may change metadata or drop members and never adds one."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.2: "A membership change is never a single-signer `supersedes` Contribution, which a rule-1 or rule-2 `withdraws` could retire without the quorum."
note: CC 3.3.4 lets a superseding family Contribution drop members, and a `supersedes` is its attester's act (CC 2.4.1); the same item then says removal is a cosigned `membership:removal` or a resignation, and CC 4.4.3.4.2 and CC 4.4.3.2.3 say no membership change is a `supersedes`. A reader of the first sentence lets one signer remove a member. The rest of the document supports CC 4.4.3.4.2; the model has "typed record supersede only".

side_a: CC 6.1.1: "MUST NOT replace `monotonic_quorum` / `revision` anti-rollback for `revocation` / `partner_record` / `org_membership`"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.3: "**`lww_skew_bounded` + `withdrawal_forward_only`**"
note: CC 6.1.1 names org_membership (and partner_record) as merged by monotonic_quorum with revision anti-rollback; CC 5.3.2.3, the home of merge policy, gives organization and org_membership latest-wins with forward-only withdrawal and has no partner_record row; CC 3.3.9 calls all three retired kinds. The hand-off in CC 6.1.1 is to CC 5.3.2.3 either way, so the outcome is that section's.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1: "`rotation_chain` is supersession lineage, not onward transfer."
side_b: CC 5.1: "an informative trail of the prior `key_grant_id`s; no row supersedes or removes a wrap"
note: One member, two descriptions: a supersession lineage in CC 2.4.1.2.1, and in CC 5.1 and CC 3.3.2 a trail under which no wrap supersedes another ("A wrap once admitted is never removed by a later one"). A reader of CC 2.4.1.2.1 alone could retire the earlier wrap.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.3: ".latest_by(asserted_at)   # signed by the user; subject_key_id = the agent occurrence"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "so revoking the newest grant never resurrects an older one"
note: ratified_pair drops withdrawn rows and then takes the latest remaining grant, so withdrawing the newest partnership grant brings back an older one under the same pair id; the boundary fold of CC 3.3.1 and CC 4.4.3.5.5 puts every earlier grant out. CC 3.3.1 states the boundary for community_trust and consent:state only, so the partnership leaves are not strictly covered.

side_a: CC 2.4.1: "This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json: "verb": "supersede"
note: Still present: the CC 2.4.1 table cell still says "by the same attester" while Part 3 has other-signer supersession (the cosigned re-bind that supersedes a bundle-seeded binding, the accord recovery signed under the recovery key, the new guardian).

side_a: CC 2.4.1: "This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester"
side_b: CC 3.2: "a new guardian's `delegates_to` carried as a `supersedes` ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)) replaces the prior binding"
note: Known and open with the steward: whether a new guardian displaces the old by their own row. Reported because this reading reaches it independently.

side_a: CC 3.1.2.1: "A rebuild is a `supersedes` on the earlier Contribution"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json provenance:build_manifest:{target} verbs: ["attest", "withdraw"]
note: Still present: the provenance families have no supersede transition and no replace verb.

side_a: CC 4.3: "on window expiry it re-routes to the live quorum"
side_b: CC 4.3: "re-routes under rule 1 to the party's other live seats and, with none, to the conferrer"
note: Who answers a deferral whose Wise Authority has lapsed: rule 1 and the `deferral:request` row of CC 3.1.9.3 send it to "the live quorum", a body; the seat rule sends it to the other seats this party conferred and then to the conferrer (for an agent, its steward), and CC 4.3 says there is no roster of Wise Authorities. A reader of rule 1 alone routes an agent's deferral to a board the steward never seated. The seat rule is the later and more specific text.

side_a: CC 1.13.2: "`consent:partnered` is theirs to revoke ([CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md))"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "A leaf with no named emitter class is unregistered, and a consumer MUST reject it"
note: CC 1.13.2, CC 4.4.3.4.3 (the agency row), CC 2.1, CC 4.5.1.1 and CC 5.3.2.2 name a dimension `consent:partnered` or `consent:partnered:{user_key}` (the agent-side stance). The closed leaf set of CC 3.3.1 has no `partnered` leaf: the pair is `consent:partnership_grant` and `consent:partnership_accept`, and `partnered` is a kind of `consent:stream`. A node following CC 5.3.2.2 emits a row a node following CC 3.3.1 rejects; and what a person revokes to end an agent's partnership is named differently in the two.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3: "The agent occurrence's withdrawal ends the binding and enters the objection path of the retirement machine"
side_b: CC 4.5.1: "**agent:** none while held — this cell is stated, not hidden"
note: CC 4.4.3.4.3 gives the agent occurrence a withdrawal that "ends the binding" and calls it "leaving"; the register's exit cell and CC 1.13.2 ("no release from stewardship") give a held agent no exit. They agree only if "the binding" is the data partnership and not the stewardship, which CC 4.4.3.4.3 does not say (its previous sentence says the accept half is signed "under the owner-binding").

side_a: CC 7.3.4: "a CIRIS agent's hold over a made thing does not loosen as that thing's capacity grows"
side_b: CC 1.13.2: "A key that cannot accept for itself is held by an accountable human who answers for it"
note: CC 7.3.4 writes the hold as a CIRIS agent's over a made thing; everywhere else the holder is an accountable human and the agent is what is held. Read literally CC 7.3.4 lets an agent be a steward. The sentence most likely means the hold over a CIRIS agent.

side_a: CC 1.16.5: "Appointment, rotation, recusal, and appeals are external to this system’s control and follow explicit anti-capture rules."
side_b: CC 4.3: "A seat over one party's deferrals is conferred by that party in a signed row and by nobody else"
note: Still present: CC 1.16.5 is unchanged, and the opening of CC 4.3 restates it ("external to this system's control") three paragraphs above the seat rule. CC 1.16.4 still transmits to "the designated Wise Authorities".

side_a: CC 3.3.13: "User-private; always `cohort_scope: self`; promotable via [CC 4.4.3.3.1](part_4_composition_governance.md)"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.3.1: "optionally morph `sub_kind`"
note: CC 3.3.13 holds a `local_data` row at self always; CC 4.4.3.3.1 makes the change of sub_kind on promotion optional, so a widened row may still be `local_data` at community or federation scope. A door that enforced "always self" would refuse the promotion CC 4.4.3.3 describes unless the sub_kind changes.
