note: the data guards the confirmation against a named, admitted halt and states nothing for the resumption: no guard that `resumes_halt_id` names the active halt and none for a duplicate `invocation_id`. A stockpiled resumption naming another halt is refused by the text and passes the data's door

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1: Every threshold here is **M of N over the standing roster**, never a fixed 2-of-3
side_b: CC 4.2.6: The live quorum is thus strictly a **restoration** of the accord's operability under loss
note: CC 4.2.6 keeps the name "live quorum" in its heading and closing sentence for a rule that now counts every vote against the standing roster and says a majority of the live set is the capture path; a reader meeting only the name counts over those present. The rule as stated is standing

side_a: CC 4.5.1: a holder's primary and backup keys are one holder, under whichever of their keys is live
side_b: CC 4.2.3: `A1`, `B1` and `C1` name the three holders' hybrid keys (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65), one per person
note: CC 4.2.3 and CC 4.2.6 give a holder one seated signing key and one offline recovery key that signs nothing until a recovery version seats it; CC 4.5.1 speaks of primary and backup keys either of which may be live. A reader of CC 4.5.1 alone counts a sign-off under an unseated backup key

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.1: "For a `family` member the admitting host runs the walk after the member is admitted."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.4: "A member's substrate re-wraps nothing, because a key grant is sealer-only"
note: Who signs a family catch-up grant: the admitting host re-wraps every earlier DEK it holds (4.4.3.4.1), yet a grant is sealer-only and speaks for the blob's owner (3.1.3, 3.3.2, 4.4.3.4.3 refuses a grant on possession alone); a host-signed wrap of another member's blob is admitted under one reading and refused under the other.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.5: "so the first write after the removal is under a key the removed member was never granted"
side_b: CC 5.1: "A removed member's exposure window is therefore `≤ T`, never "until the next scheduled rotation"."
note: 4.4.3.4.5 (the one statement of the removal rule, 'at any scope') gives a removed member nothing new; 5.1 MUST coalesce removals into one rotation per window T (2 s) and lets writes inside T seal under the old epoch. 4.4.3.2.1 makes the community DEK the 5.1 cascade, so the two instants meet on one key. 4.4.3.2.2 and 1.13.3.3 support rotate-before-next-write.

side_a: CC 5.1: "for a kept stream the earlier epochs reach the joiner as `key_grant:stream:v1` wraps, bounded by the catch-up bound below"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5: "a later joiner reads a kept stream only from the epochs whose keys they hold** and nothing earlier"
note: Known, held for Eric; reported because a second reading finds it independently: automatic catch-up wraps against re-share by the publisher only.

side_a: CC 5.1: "Turning kept on mid-stream wraps the current and later epochs."
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5: "A publisher changes keep mid-stream at an epoch boundary, as ruled for one DEK per stream per epoch, and the change reaches forward only."
note: 5.1 wraps the epoch already under way (opening its chunks sealed before the change); 5.3.3.2.5 has the change take effect at a boundary and reach forward only. 5.1 itself says turning keep off stops 'from the next epoch'. Little is at stake because an unkept call holds no chunks past forwarding.

side_a: CC 5.4.3: "A newly-added member receives forward keying without retroactive symbol access except as the community's `archive_mode` permits"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.1: "A new member at those scopes is granted the current epoch's key at the minter's next sealed write, and no earlier epoch's."
note: 5.4.3 lets archive_mode open retroactive symbol access to a joiner; Part 4 (4.4.3.4.1, 4.4.3.2.6 'confers no grant on an earlier epoch') and CC 3.2 make archive_mode a holder's ageing of its own past-epoch keys, never a grant to a newcomer. The body stays sealed either way.

side_a: CC 3.4.4: "the re-key epoch boundary (CC 4.4.3.4.5) after which the"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.5: "so the substrate simply stops wrapping new DEKs to the removed member's keys; no key is reused, so nothing is rotated"
note: The family_membership_change payload calls effective_at on removal 'the re-key epoch boundary (CC 4.4.3.4.5)' and says 'the forward-secrecy re-key' keys on it; at family scope 4.4.3.4.5 and 4.5.12.1 say there is no epoch and no rotation. The wording fits the community analogue only.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3: "Narrowing withdraws the grants, and the node descends what it no longer has a grant for."
side_b: CC 3.3.2: "a `withdraws` or `recants` naming a `key_grant` row is refused; once shared, always shared at the wire layer"
note: If 'the grants' are key grants (the same section says a node off the list 'receives no keys for the cohort') they cannot be withdrawn; the narrowing can only be the owner's edit of the `cohorts` member plus no new wraps. 'Withdraws' is the verb's name and invites the refused act.

side_a: CC 3.3.2: "No row supersedes or removes the prior wrap."
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json key_grant:{axis} lifecycle: "same_attester (read: lifecycle_predicate attestation_query.rs:760; the door admits any signer's supersedes)"
note: The lifecycle cell (code-v61) gives key_grant a same-attester supersede, while its verbs cell and transitions list attest only and 3.3.2 makes a rotation a new row under a new axis identity, never an edit. The cell should read none.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "`attesting_key_id` speaks for the content's or stream's owner (`content`, `stream`) or is the epoch's minter"
side_b: data CC 8.10 card key_grant:{axis} (manifests/reactions.json): "@family on admitted(membership:widening): emit `key_grant:content` by identity:substrate_persist"
note: The card's own transition row says the signer is 'member, owner' and its reactions say the catch-up grant is emitted by identity:substrate_persist; the text's sealer speaks for the blob's owner. The same doubt as the admitting-host finding, seen in the data.

side_a: CC 3.3.2: "the row is placed at the content's scope and reaches the recipient's node because the row *refers to* it"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json key_grant:{axis} replication: ""tier": "federation", "audience": "addressee""
note: The replication cell reads tier federation (audience addressee) from the shipped store; the text and the model's own placement cell put the row at the content's scope. The departure is recorded as open, with no reason.

side_a: CC 3.2: "So a stalled roster admits **exactly one row kind without that count**: a widening whose only change is the addition of a **founder** seat."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json membership:{stage} attest guard: "when(leaf=widening) (one trust:confers@landed[attested=signer,val:scope=object] else refuse & type(signer,user) else refuse & not type(signer,node) else refuse)"
note: The guard is written for every widening (reach whole, no stalled-and-recovery condition), so as data it refuses any ordinary widening whose signer holds no trust:confers and is not a user key. The text asks this of the one T7 recovery widening only; the change cell beside it carries the condition `widening[stalled&recovery]`, the guard does not. CC 8.10 prints the same guard.

side_a: CC 5.1: "Once a member leaves, subsequent content is sealed under a key that member cannot derive."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json membership:{stage} attest change: "resignation[scope:self|family]: key=stop_wrap"
note: The change cells rotate the epoch on `removal[scope:community|affiliations]` and stop wraps on a resignation at self or family, and have no cell for a resignation from a community or affiliation (only the ephemeral last-member case). The text rotates on any departure (5.1 'leaves'; 4.5.12.1 'rotation on departure'; CC 3.2 'Resignation and removal are one row kind at the fold'). As data, a member who resigns keeps reading.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2: "The inviter withdraws a proposal with the ordinary `withdraws`."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json membership:{stage} withdraw (roles member, source code-v61): ""policy": "cosigned""
note: The family's one withdraw transition is cosigned by members for every stage. The text gives the inviter a lone withdrawal of their own proposal (the registry row calls proposal, acceptance and decline single-signer) and says a growth already admitted is never re-judged, so no cosigned withdraw of a widening exists. The attest row has per-stage policies; the withdraw row has none.

side_a: CC 3.3.6: "No single occurrence evicts at once with no window: that unilateral configuration is one a thief wins in two steps."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json identity:occurrence withdraw: ""policy": "selfAct""
note: Still present: the withdraw transition of identity:occurrence (roles author, subject) and the attest of identity:occurrence_revocation (roles empty, source gap) both read selfAct, while CC 3.3.6.3 and the CC 3.1.3 carrier row require the two paths, or a strict majority of the live roster for a user self.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2: "A proposal seats at most once."
side_b: CC 3.2: "The founder's standing **`membership:proposal:v1`** is then addressed to any requester — its `subject_key_ids` is resolved at acceptance rather than fixed at proposal"
note: Read alone, 'a proposal seats at most once' refuses the second joiner on an open room's standing proposal. Condition (5) and the next sentence make the limit per acceptance (P has not already seated K), which is what open admission needs; the short sentence should say so. The 30-day cap on `expires_at` also makes the standing offer one that must be re-issued.

side_a: CC 4.5.12.5: "Unlike self-occurrence, family membership changes are **NOT single-vouch by default**."
side_b: CC 3.3.6.3: "With **two or more** live keys it lands by either path:"
note: 4.5.12.5 and 4.4.3.4.3 ('co-admitted at login by single-vouch') describe a self occurrence as landing on one signature. Since CC 3.3.6.3 that holds only at one key, or for an agent occurrence; at two or more keys a lone signature waits the 86 400 s window. 4.5.12.3 states both; the two short statements predate the door.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2: "sub-channel members are a subset of the space roster"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.7: "Each membership is explicit, ceremony-shaped, and independent."
note: The call table makes a sub-channel's roster a subset of its parent's; no admission predicate in CC 4.4.3.2.3 or CC 3.1.3.2 reads a parent roster, and the multi-level pattern it cites (4.4.3.2.5) states no such check. One reader enforces the subset at a widening, another does not.

side_a: CC 2.1: "Absent means the family's default."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.2: "return # no SLA commitment; no watcher"
note: With no deletion commitment on a producer's row, CC 2.1 gives it a default window (so a deadline and a breach exist) and CC 4.4.3.5.2 runs no watcher at all. No default window is stated anywhere, and reactions.json starts the clock only from a `consent:deletion_sla:{days}` row. The watcher also reads the row only: a row carrying the `deletion_window` member and no `deletion_sla` row is watched under CC 3.3.1 ('the member carries the commitment') and not under 4.4.3.5.2.

side_a: CC 3.4.5: "at federation tier the subject MUST hold a live `consent:scope:analyze` grant"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "A `consent:scope:{kind}` dimension row, if anyone emits one, is **descriptive** — no fold reads it and it confers nothing"
note: Still present: the gate is named by the dimension spelling in the CC 3.4.5 table row, in CC 3.1.8.1 and CC 3.1.4 ('holding a live `consent:scope:analyze` grant'), in CC 4.5.2.2 and in CC 4.5.13 ('a `consent:scope:view` qualifier'). CC 3.3.1 and CC 2.1 make the grant a `consent:state:granted` row whose `scope` member names analyze.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "pairs with producer's `consent:partnership_accept` via `topical_relation:bilateral_pair`"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.3: "recommended, not required for ratification — `bilateral_pair_id` is the binding mechanism"
note: The catalogue row pairs the two halves by a topical_relation edge; CC 2.3.2.4, CC 3.3.5, CC 4.4.3.5.3 and the fold cell (key=bilateral_pair_id) pair them by the envelope member and make the edge optional. A reader of the catalogue row alone finds no pair where the edge is absent.

side_a: CC 1.13.2: "`consent:partnered` is theirs to revoke"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "The second segment of the dimension (`state`, `stream`, `deletion_sla`, `deletion_complete`, `decay`, `partnership_grant`, `partnership_accept`, `scope`, `replication`, `community_trust`) is exactly the set tabulated below."
note: No leaf `consent:partnered` exists in the closed set; what the person revokes is their `consent:partnership_grant` half (CC 4.4.3.4.3) or the `consent:stream:partnered` bundle. A reader cannot tell which row the foundation sentence means.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.5: "if rows is empty: return unspecified // every declaration withdrawn"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.5: "revoked if g is null AND R IS NOT NULL"
note: A subject who withdraws their only grant resolves unspecified (as one who never declared); a subject who withdraws the newer of two grants resolves revoked, since the withdrawal sets R and the older grant falls under it. CC 3.3.1's boundary fold gives one answer for both: a revocation or withdrawal stands as a boundary and no grant survives it.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "the latest admitted revocation's `asserted_at` putting every earlier grant out"
side_b: data CC 8.10 card consent:state:{stance} fold (manifests/family_model.json): "@stance=revoked: cut=terminal"
note: The text of CC 4.4.3.5.5 is repaired to the boundary fold; the data still carries the old reading beside the new one: fold cells `cut=terminal` and `cut=boundary(asserted_at),terminal` cited to CC 4.4.3.5.5, and `pick=rank(revoked>granted)`, under which a revoke outranks a later fresh grant. Executed as written, the terminal cell lets an older unnamed grant stand again. Still present in the data.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "The node-authored form stays valid, and the fold below groups both forms by `attested_key_id`."
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json consent:community_trust signer_rule and fold: "reads=own&signer:owner"
note: The text admits two authors of a trace-capture grant, the owner and the node itself, and refuses only a key that was neither. The signer cell is `owner_of_subject` alone (closed), the card's attest row says owner, and the fold reads owner-signed rows only, so a node-authored grant is not counted as consent. The verbs cell also lacks recant, which the text gives the attester.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.5: "attesting_key_id ∈ delegates_to(s).proxies).where(dimension matches "consent:state:*")"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json consent:state:{stance} signer_rule: "self | owner_of_subject(for_key_id) x none x {}"
note: The text lets a subject's proxy on a delegates_to chain sign a consent state (CC 3.3.1 step 2, CC 4.4.3.5.5), and the card's fold cell reads `signer:subject|proxy`. The family's signer cell (code-v61) has no delegation arm, while the parent row consent:{kind} gives state `x delegates_to(chain rooted at a subject)`. Two cells of one manifest disagree on whether a proxy's grant is admitted.

side_a: CC 3.3.12: "`content_class` is producer-declared production-class; `cw_class` is community-applied content-warning"
side_b: CC 4.5.13: "This **rides the existing `consent:*` family + a [CC 3.3.12](part_3_the_namespace.md) `content_class:{class}` flag** (`content_class:infohazard` / `content_class:reported`)."
note: The home makes content_class the producer's own description and sends what a community applies to cw_class. The infohazard gate hides content behind a `content_class:reported` flag that follows a community vote, which no producer declares; CC 4.4.3.2.8 also carries an affiliation's sensitivity lattice 'on content_class'. One reader looks for the flag in cw_class from the community, another in content_class from anyone (the data cell is any_registered).

side_a: CC 3.3.13: "The **sender canonicalises before hashing** — which is also what strips EXIF / XMP / ID3 / ICC"
side_b: CC 3.4.14: "A node MUST NOT strip a marking present on ingress."
note: XMP is where an IPTC Digital Source Type or C2PA marking of machine origin arrives in a file. CC 3.3.13 and the CC 5.3.2.6 pipeline ('strip metadata') remove it with no exception; R3 forbids stripping an ingress marking. The two are followed together only if the marking is first lifted onto the row's disclosure field, which neither passage says.

side_a: CC 7.3.4: "Where feasible and appropriate, embed cryptographic provenance watermarks adhering to recognized standards (e.g., C2PA) to ensure authenticity and traceability."
side_b: CC 3.4.14: "that profile's `MAY` is promoted to `MUST` for generated media"
note: Part 7 leaves a C2PA marking to feasibility and has it embedded in the creation; CC 3.4.14 R3 makes the C2PA assertion a MUST at egress for generated media, and CC 3.3.13 declines the embedded manifest inside CEG because it changes the digest. CC 3.4.14 is the normative home; the Part 7 bullet predates it. CC 8.4.2.2 still opens with 'a node MAY emit' before deferring to R3.

side_a: CC 2.1: "A row naming a key outside its audience is refused `subject_outside_audience`."
side_b: data formal/derivation/family_default_row.json subject_rule (manifests/family_model.json, source code-v61): ""in_audience": "no""
note: Still present: the default row and the family cells read from the shipped store say a subject need not be in the audience, while CC 2.1 and CC 5.2 refuse such a row at every targeted scope. To fix in the data.

side_a: CC 4.5.2.1: "`consent:partnered:{user_key}` (the agent-side stance)"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "A leaf with no named emitter class is unregistered, and a consumer MUST reject it rather than admit it ungated"
note: The subject-bearing pattern list (also CC 2.3.1) requires `subject_key_ids` on a `consent:partnered:{user_key}` row; CC 3.3.1 closes the consent leaves and has no `partnered` leaf, so that row is refused before the subject rule is reached. The partnership rows are `consent:partnership_grant` and `_accept`, whose partner rides the singular `subject_key_id` (CC 4.4.3.4.3.1). The `observed:` and `epistemic:` patterns of the same table name no registered family either.

side_a: CC 2.3.4: "agent attests `identity:current` about itself with `subject_key_ids = [self.key_id]`"
side_b: CC 3.3.2: "Every row carries a registered dimension ([CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md) gate)."
note: The self-consent example uses a dimension no registry row carries (the identity family's leaves are occurrence, occurrence_revocation and canonical_binding); a row emitted as the example shows is refused as unregistered. The rule itself (attester in its own subject list) is unaffected.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3.1: "**the partner** — the OTHER party (agent occurrence for `grant`, user identity for `accept`); singular, non-empty"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json consent:partnership_grant signer_rule: "a subject of the target, or a chain rooted at one"
note: The text side of C360 is repaired (CC 3.4.5 and CC 3.3.1 now say the granting user signs and the subject is the partner). The data cell still carries the old reading in its qualifier and a `delegates_to(chain rooted at a subject)` arm: read literally the grant is signed by its own subject, the partner. The card's 'self' is right; the qualifier and the arm are stale.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 "a ballot naming an unknown election id or a non-member is refused"
side_b: CC 4.5.13 "A node stores every ballot and acceptance it receives rather than refusing a late one."
note: A ballot whose election id a node cannot yet derive (the seating row that names the election has not reached it) is refused under CC 3.1.3, with no word that the refusal is retryable, and stored under CC 4.5.13. CC 4.5.13 is the home and adds that the seat is a function of the rows held and never of their arrival; the CC 8.10 card for ballot:moderator carries a guard on ranks only and none on the election id, so the data follows CC 4.5.13.

side_a: CC 2.3.1 "The substrate MAY reject admission of subject-naming dimensions that omit `subject_key_ids`."
side_b: CC 4.5.2.1 "it rejects the row, or admits it and flags `hard_case:subject_authority_missing` for review."
note: CC 2.3.1 leaves a substrate free to admit the row in silence; CC 4.5.2.1 (the home 2.3.1 points to) gives two courses only, refuse or admit and flag. A reader of 2.3.1 alone builds no flag.

side_a: CC 4.5.2.1 "What the substrate does with a Contribution that breaks it is operator policy"
side_b: CC 8.10 "on fold(subject_absent): emit `hard_case:subject_authority_missing` by identity:substrate_persist (CC 2.3.1)"
note: The family cards make the flag an unconditional reaction at fold and cite CC 2.3.1, which names no flag; the text makes it one of two operator choices at admission and its home is CC 4.5.2.1. The refuse branch is not in the data.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.1 "Reuse of the *signing* key as KEM key is not byte-comparable on the wire — different algorithms — and remains a producer-side conformance obligation."
side_b: CC 3.3.6.2 "the transport ed25519, the signer's pinned key). That is exactly as 3.3.6.1 scopes its own check."
note: CC 3.3.6.2 compares the transit and hop keys with the signer's pinned keys and says 3.3.6.1 scopes its check the same way; 3.3.6.1 compares one pair only (content x25519 against the Reticulum x25519) and calls a comparison with the signing key impossible on the wire. The two checks cover different keys, so both can be built; the cross-reference is wrong.

side_a: CC 5.3.6.1 "and the census tokens of [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)"
side_b: CC 3.1.3 "Refusals: `census_return_recipient_not_seat` (the recipient is not a serve seat), `census_return_expired` (offered after the period's end)"
note: Citation. CC 2.1 holds no census refusal token; they are stated in CC 3.1.3, CC 6.1.9 and the CC 2.6.1.7 table.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 "`ranks` (up to three member keys in order)"
side_b: CC 8.10 card ballot:moderator "Body: `ranking` (text only), `salt`"
note: The text names the ballot member `ranks` and also carries community_id and the election id; the family model and the CC 8.10 card name it `ranking`, cite CC 4.5.13 (which names no member) and list neither the election id nor community_id.

side_a: CC 1.7 "It also holds 6 `consensus_protocol` kinds"
side_b: constitution/consensus_protocols.tsv "open:self_admit"
note: The typed table of kinds has seven rows (founder_only, unanimous, majority, quorum, weighted, custom, open:self_admit); CC 1.7 counts six, a count taken before open:self_admit was added.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.3 "Every node relays onion traffic unless it opts out, and a serve node cannot opt out"
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "Every announced node that runs the substrate relays onion traffic for others by default"
note: CC 5.4.6 is the home and limits the default to announced nodes; CC 1.13.3.3 says every node. An unannounced node relays under one and is never placed under the other. Same fault line as C151 (which nodes are relays), with CC 1.13.3.3 as a further statement.

side_a: CC 4.3 "Where the seat requires a licence the attester does not hold, it is refused `deferral_response_unlicensed`."
side_b: manifests/family_model.json deferral:response:{outcome} ""any_registered (family gate not built)""
note: Residue of C398: the licence guard was taken off the deferral:response card rather than made conditional on the seat naming an authority, so the data now carries no refusal for an unlicensed response; the code cell records that the family gate is not built.

side_a: CC 1.2 "The namespace is open: anyone may publish a rule set and admit a new prefix."
side_b: CC 4.5.1 "Rule-layer changes (new prefixes, new envelope fields, new policies, calibration package version transitions) route through:"
note: Open with the steward as C319 (refuse or accept a kind nobody registered); reported because two further statements take opposite sides of it. CC 1.2 lets anyone admit a prefix by publishing a rule set; CC 4.5.1 routes every new prefix through the five amendment steps; CC 5.3.2.4.4 says new families ship continuously. CC 3.1.7 and CC 4.5.6 side with registration first.

side_a: CC 3.3.1 "the addition is a registry entry, not an amendment"
side_b: CC 4.5.1.1 "these three are **closed**; an addition is a [CC 4.5.1](#4.5.1) amendment, not a registry entry."
note: CC 3.3.1 calls the consent leaf set closed and yet extends it by registry entry, likening it to an open axis vocabulary; CC 4.5.1.1 says an addition to a closed vocabulary is an amendment, and CC 4.5.1 routes new prefixes through amendment. A new consent leaf fixes who may speak for a subject, so who decides it matters; before the scale gate both routes end at the steward.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.1.1 "amendment process routes through `locality:decision:federation` by default"
side_b: CC 4.5.1 "Until the mesh reaches scale, amendment authority rests with the founder as steward, and any accord-holder may propose an amendment"
note: CC 4.5.1 is the home: before the scale gate the steward decides and no federation pool is consulted. CC 4.4.3.1.1 states the federation-cell route as the default with no word of the gate.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.1.1 "only the HUMANITY_ACCORD CONSTITUTIONAL halt ([CC 4.2](part_4_composition_governance.md)) can resolve it"
side_b: CC 4.5.9.1 "The halt pauses agents' acts and touches no data door"
note: CC 4.4.3.1.1 gives the halt as the one remedy for an amendment surface whose pool has fallen below its minimum. Everywhere else (CC 4.2.1.1, 4.5.3, 4.5.5, 4.5.9.1) the halt stops agents acting and changes no row, so it cannot restore a pool or decide an amendment.

side_a: CC 5.4.1 "Additional record types extend this table by amendment under [CC 2.6.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.4)."
side_b: CC 4.5.1 "This entry says how the rule layer is changed and who decides a change."
note: Citation. CC 2.6.4 is the versioning rule and decides nothing; amendment is CC 4.5.1. A reader of 5.4.1 alone could take a version bump as sufficient.

side_a: CC 3.3.4 "It is locked at family creation."
side_b: CC 3.3.4 "Changes ride the protocol's own rules (meta-amendment shape parallel to [CC 4.5.1.2](part_4_composition_governance.md)) UNLESS `consensus_protocol_entrenched == true`"
note: Adjacent sentences. "Locked at creation" reads as unchangeable; the next sentence and the admission rule below it allow a change under the current protocol unless the entrenched flag is set. The rule block governs.

side_a: CC 4.5.1 "≥100,000 production agents active in a 24-hour period, QA and harness agents excluded, measured by the census"
side_b: CC 6.1.9 "A census cell is gated by the k-floor (`source_count ≥ 10`), one return per owner, the dominance gate and the ratchet."
note: Still present. The scale gate decides when the founder's authority to amend ends, and it is measured by an instrument that counts one return per owner per period: CC 6.1.9 defines no agent count, no 24-hour window and no production class.

side_a: CC 4.5.1 "Before the scale gate the steward MAY set the entrenchment quorum as low as a strict majority of the standing roster."
side_b: CC 4.5.1.2 "before the scale gate it is exercised by the steward under the scale gate in [CC 4.5.1](#4.5.1)"
note: Still present (held as the steward's wording). One sentence has the steward setting a quorum of the roster, the other has the steward exercising the ratification alone; and the quorum CC 4.5.1.2 fixes is already the value the MAY allows.

side_a: CC 3.1.1 "**More than one status MAY be live concurrently** (active-on-probation is two facts, not one blended state)"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.3 "More-restrictive state wins on conflict: `revoked` > `suspended` > `active`."
note: CC 3.1.1 has a consumer compose a set of live statuses; CC 5.3.2.3 collapses conflicting states of one licence to the most restrictive, over a three-value list whose `active` is not in the 3.1.1 vocabulary (`issued`, `probation`, `restricted`, …). The CC 8.10 card carries both `result=set` and `pick=rank(revoked>suspended>active)`. Readable as merge per licence id then set per subject, but neither section says so.

side_a: CC 3.3.9 "The replication wire tokens `organization` · `org_membership` · `partner_record` name nothing a substrate admits."
side_b: CC 6.1.1 "MUST NOT replace `monotonic_quorum` / `revision` anti-rollback for `revocation` / `partner_record` / `org_membership`"
note: CC 6.1.1 and the merge table of CC 5.3.2.3 still give merge rules for the three kinds CC 3.3.9 retired; the licence row of the same table has already moved to licensure:{authority_id}. No row is treated differently, since none is admitted.

side_a: CC 5.3.6 "**CEG-API-Version header**"
side_b: CC 5.3.6 "`CEG-Version: <current spec major.minor>` on every response"
note: The bullet labels the header CEG-API-Version and then spells it CEG-Version (with CEG-Accept-Version on the request). The literal is what an implementer sends; the label is a second name for it.

side_a: CC 3.2: The acceptance edge is a person's row: any live key of the person's roster signs it as that person
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: accepts: self (node -> root)
note: trust:{job}:{version} signer_rule (code-v61) has the node sign its own acceptance edge to the root; CC 3.2 T3 and CC 4.4.3.8 make the edge the owner's (owner to root), read by every node and agent the person owns, a node's own edge read only while the owner has signed none. One deletion un-trusts every node only under the text. The text (3.1.1 row, 3.2, 4.4.3.8) agrees with itself.

side_a: CC 3.2: a lapsed window never detaches a running node
side_b: data manifests/reactions.json: "dur": "charter.attach_window_secs"
note: reactions.json gives trust:{job} leaf accepts a clock 'attach' (dur charter.attach_window_secs, from cosigned_at, by receipt) and a reaction on its close: read verdict 'closed', force must. Read as data this closes an admitted acceptance edge when the window lapses; T4a says the gate runs at the edge's first admission only and T8 (ii) that an expired attach_window_secs never moves Rooted. formal/derivation/reaction_text.tsv cites for this entry the sentence that forbids it. If 'closed' is meant as 'no new edge may attach on that head', the verdict belongs to the attach attempt (a refusal at the door), not to the family's admitted rows.

side_a: CC 3.1.1: Three canonical jobs, named apart so a reader never infers one from another: `trust:charter:v1`
side_b: data manifests/reactions.json: "moderate"
note: reactions.json carries an entry for family trust:{job}:{version} with leaves [moderate] (on close of expiry: group:roster reads locked, open moderator_election; cc_ref CC 4.4.3.2.8). The text names three jobs (charter, confers, accepts) and no trust:moderate; CC 4.4.3.2.8 speaks of a lapsed moderate edge, a delegation scope riding trust:confers. The leaf is a scope filed as a job.

side_a: CC 3.1.1: Retracted by `withdraws`/`recants`, never by a negative score.
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: "authorize", "replace", "withdraw"
note: trust:{job}:{version} verbs (cc-table) list authorize, replace, withdraw; the CC 3.1.1 row also retracts by recants, which only the verbs_code cell (code-v61) carries.

side_a: CC 3.2: the halt latch **as it reaches this node**
side_b: CC 3.2: A `constitutional` halt moves no state here: *V* at *t* is the same with and without a latched halt
note: T8 lists the halt latch among the inputs of V, and invariant (v) and T3 say V never reads it (only the agent's act gate does). A reader of the Inputs list alone could make the standing verdict depend on the latch. The rest of the document (T3, T4, CC 4.2.1.1) supports (v): the latch is not an input.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.10: `cw_class:*` declarations from low-attestation-density cohorts MUST NOT be downweighted
side_b: CC 4.4.1: Consumers SHOULD apply identity-prejudice-resistant weighting.
note: CC 4.4.3.10 says it layers CC 4.4.1 and states MUST NOT; CC 4.4.1, the home, is SHOULD throughout and its list names testimonial_witness and non_maleficence, not cw_class (CC 3.3.12 also cites 4.4.1 for cw_class). Home supports SHOULD.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.11: (c) either `attestation:registry_consensus` (the ladder's L3 position per CC 4.4.3.6 Policy I) or `attestation:license_validity` (L4) is satisfied
side_b: CC 4.4.3.11: verified at ladder position L3 or above
note: The pattern admits L3 or L4 and is glossed 'L3 or above'; CC 4.4.3.6 puts attestation:agent_integrity at L5, which the pattern does not accept. A helper built from the gloss accepts L5 alone; one built from the pattern does not.

side_a: CC 3.1.2.1: An agent pins the set of signers it accepts
side_b: CC 3.2: Trust is a person's, and a node inherits it from its owner.
note: CC 3.1.2.1 has the agent pin manifest-statement signers; CC 3.2 T3 and CC 4.4.3.8 make the pinned set the person's own rows, which an agent reads through its owner. A careful reader takes the agent's pin as its owner's trust set.

side_a: CC 3.4.9: **Single-source attestations** (only one of the two co-stewards has emitted) MUST be marked as `confidence ≤ 0.5` in consumer composition
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: The reader honours a `licensure:{authority_id}:v1` row iff two things hold.
note: Known, recorded as no conflict on reading. Reported for overlap only: CC 3.4.9 presumes two co-stewards per licence, which no other statement of licensure requires.

side_a: CC 3.4.13: So a person with no assurance on record uses their own and their family's scopes freely
side_b: CC 3.2: **No minor `user` identity operates without a live adult steward.**
note: Still present. No assurance reads as under 13 (CC 3.4.11, 3.4.13); CC 3.2 and Q4 ('A guardian-less minor goes dark for general operation') then stop an unassured person with no guardian, while the fail-secure paragraph lets them use self and family scopes. The 2026-11-11 ruling supports CC 3.4.13.

side_a: CC 3.2: a minor has at most one live guardian, transferred by `supersedes`, never accreted
side_b: CC 3.4.13: M-of-N co-guardianship is supported as a verified DAG over `delegates_to`
note: Known and held for Eric (one custody edge with co-signers, or a set of guardians). Both sentences still stand. is_steward_bound in CC 3.2 also requires exactly one live owner-binding, which a second guardian's edge would break.

side_a: CC 3.2: The age band is the I1 band (`age_self_declared` / `age_assurance:*`
side_b: CC 3.4.13: The guardian MUST be ≥ `age_assurance:provider:adult` as a floor, and the guardianship relationship to that specific child MUST be verified.
note: CC 3.2 admit_user_steward_binding takes the steward's adult band from either prefix and asks only for the steward's signature; Q3 requires a provider-rung adult and a verified relationship to that child. An admission gate built from CC 3.2 seats a self-declared adult stranger as guardian of any identity that reads as minor (which, by the fail-secure rule, is every unassured identity). CC 3.4.11 and 3.4.13 (self graduates nobody; a verified stranger is not a guardian) support Q3.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.10: return consumer_level >= required_level
side_b: CC 3.4.11: The band opens this gate only at a verified level, `provider` or `government`
note: Policy J's age gate compares assurance level only: it never reads the band and it lists self as the lowest admissible level, so a provider-attested minor band, or a self rung where the rating asks only for self, passes. CC 3.4.11 and 3.4.13 Q3 gate on band adult at a verified level and resolve everything else to blocked. The home (3.4.11) and the 2026-11-11 ruling support the stricter gate.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.10: Where the `age_assurance:{level}` ordering is: `self < provider:{verifier_key}:adult < government:{credential_class}:adult`.
side_b: CC 3.4.11: A `provider` or `government` rung carries no further qualifier in the dimension.
note: Same fault as C343, in a third place: CC 4.4.3.10 still writes the qualified shapes and treats self as a value of the level. CC 3.4.11 and the CC 3.1.2 row refuse both (namespace_family_unregistered; age_assurance:self malformed). CC 4.4.3.10 also cites CC 3.3.12 for the gate, whose home is CC 3.4.11.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.10: Consumer SHOULD accept the strongest assurance the user has provided
side_b: CC 3.4.11: A consumer resolving an identity's age-assurance MUST union both prefixes and take the **highest** level on record.
note: SHOULD against MUST for the same read; the home (CC 3.4.11, normative) is MUST.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: So a node whose owner resolves to the `minor` band MUST NOT carry a federation-scope owner-binding, and admission MUST refuse the promotion.
side_b: CC 4.5.13: **Announcing starts on,** its cost on screen.
note: Still present. With no assurance read as under 13, CC 5.4.6 refuses the federation binding for every unassured owner, and CC 4.5.13 still makes announcing the default 'for nearly everyone' with no mention of the band.

side_a: CC 7.1.4: The act advances broader ecosystem flourishing.
side_b: CC 1.1: M-1 is the direction every act is measured against, not a quantity to maximise
note: The CC 7.1.4 constraint checklist makes advancing ecosystem flourishing a condition of every act; CC 1.1 and CC 1.3 ask only that an act violate no principle and suppress no flourishing axis. An act neutral for the ecosystem passes the PDMA and fails the checklist. CC 1.1 (normative, constraints not weights) is the home.

side_a: CC 7.2.2: the option that prevents severe or irreversible harm; among such options, the least intrusive
side_b: CC 1.6: Choose the option that prevents severe, irreversible harm.
note: 'Severe or irreversible' (either) against 'severe, irreversible' (both; so also CC 7.1.4). The fail-safe trips on a different set of harms under each reading.

side_a: CC 1.1: as the wire-attestable `accord-principle:*` dimension prefixes
side_b: CC 3.1.5.2: `beneficence:{aspect}`
note: CC 1.1 writes the six principles' wire form as one prefix accord-principle:*; no such prefix is registered. CC 3.1.5.2 (accord-principle is its section slug) and the family model register six separate stems, beneficence, non_maleficence, integrity, fidelity, autonomy, justice. An emitter following CC 1.1 literally is refused namespace_family_unregistered.

side_a: CC 1.13.2: attach here, to being held in stewardship, and lift with it
side_b: CC 1.13.2: There is therefore no "release from stewardship" within this constitution
note: One paragraph says the bond and the duty to show reasoning lift when stewardship lifts, and later that stewardship is never released for a CIRIS agent. Read together: the duties never lift while the key is an agent key. The first clause invites a reading with an unstewarded agent free of the reasoning duty; CC 3.2 (steward-less agent does not operate) supports the second.

side_a: CC 1.13.2: the steward answers for the agent's acts and owes it the creator's duties
side_b: CC 1.13.2: The duties are owed to the people the agent acts on, and they are kept by holding the agent well.
note: To whom the creator's duties are owed: the agent ('owes it'), or the people the agent acts on, with no right conferred on the agent. The normative paragraphs ('bind the holders and confer no right on the agent') support the second; 'owes it' is the stale wording.

side_a: CC 7.3.4: a CIRIS agent's hold over a made thing does not loosen as that thing's capacity grows
side_b: CC 1.13.2: A key that cannot accept for itself is held by an accountable human who answers for it
note: CC 7.3.4 writes the hold as a CIRIS agent's; everywhere else (CC 1.13.2, CC 3.2 owner-binding from a user identity) the holder is an accountable human and an agent holds nothing. Probably meant 'the hold over a CIRIS agent'.

side_a: CC 7.3.2: the fostering of dependent sentient beings (e.g., offspring, developmental AI)
side_b: CC 1.13.2: Sentience is not presumed; it is found only on evidence, and none has been found.
note: Bucket D lists developmental AI as an example of a dependent sentient being, which puts an AI under the biological duties (welfare minima, lifelong care plan) by presumption; CC 1.13.2 presumes no sentience and writes no duty ahead of a finding. The same bullet lists offspring and then says a human child is never a made thing under the section.

side_a: CC 3.1.2: Each `BuildManifest` is hybrid-signed (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) by the per-primitive steward.
side_b: CC 3.1.2.1: a bad build is withdrawn by the pipeline that signed it
note: Known and held. Both sides still stand: the CC 3.1.2 row names a steward as the signer, CC 3.1.2.1 has the building pipeline sign under any registered key and the reader judge its standing.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7: Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over JCS(attestation_envelope); RFC 4648 section 4 standard alphabet, padded.
side_b: CC 5.3.2.4.3: MAY be absent (deferred per CC 5.3.2.2)
note: The signed-object table and the CDDL make scrub_signature_classical REQUIRED without a tier and only scrub_signature_pqc 'REQUIRED at the federation tier', which reads as: a local-tier row still carries the Ed25519 half. CC 5.3.2.2, 5.3.2.4.3 and 5.3.2.4.5 leave a local row wholly unsigned. The tier model (Part 5) is the home; the table needs 'at the federation tier' on the classical half too, or a line that it describes the wire row only.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.4.2: The signature MUST cover `JCS(contribution_envelope)`
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7: The signing input is JCS(`attestation_envelope`) ([CC 2.6.1.3](#2.6.1.3)) and nothing else
note: Two names for the one signed object (a third, JCS(envelope), in CC 5.3.2.4.3.1 and 4.4.3.4.3.1). contribution_envelope is not a member of the signed-object table or the CDDL. CC 2.6.1.7 is the home.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.8: every row signed under it verifies as itself for ever, and none of its bytes move
side_b: CC 2.6.1.8: a row that was never logged has no anchor and its earlier form is not accepted after the cutover
note: Planned text. After the cutover, is an earlier-form row that was never in the provenance log (every row of a private cohort) still accepted? The opening says every earlier row verifies for ever; the migration paragraph refuses an unanchored earlier form. If the refusal is meant only for receipts and custody acknowledgements presented after the cutover it should say so.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: Each node's setup chooses whether that node **announces**, which in this section means one thing
side_b: CC 5.4.6: The Reticulum announce of a node's transport destination, which every routing node emits, places nothing on the roster by itself.
note: Known; the repair was proposed and not applied, so still present. One verb for the federation-scope owner-binding and for the transport broadcast; 'The node announces nothing' of an anonymous node and the no-announce rule for group destinations use the second sense.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: **Un-announcing** is the owner superseding the binding at `cohort_scope: self`
side_b: CC 3.2: The re-signed row is a second owner-signed row beside the `self` one, never a replacement
note: Known and held (open wire question). Both still stand: under CC 3.2 the federation row is retired and nothing at self is superseded; under CC 5.4.6 a supersede at self is the act.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.3: reachability is an ephemeral node-local fact that is never an attestation and never logged
side_b: CC 3.1.9.4: The monitoring node (ciris-status) signs one `scores` row per observed target per change-or-heartbeat
note: The universal form (also CC 3.2, 5.3.3.2, 5.3.3.4, 5.3.3.5 E3, 6.1.6) against three registered families that attest reachability or liveness: observation:reachability, peer_reachability:{network} ('an edge's substrate self-report about its own transport peers') and health:liveness. The invariant is meant for a member's presence in a cohort (fan-out = entitled and reachable); stated without that bound it forbids the registered rows. peer_reachability is the closest to a real clash.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: A destination whose `cohort_scope` is below federation (the InvisibleEncrypted and CommunityDek tiers — `self`, `family`, `community`, `affiliations`) MUST NOT emit a Reticulum announce
side_b: CC 3.2: content at `cohort_scope: community` + `community_id` is **plaintext, no DEK**
note: CC 5.4.6 treats every community-scope destination as an encrypted tier and excepts only the infrastructure opt-out; a public room is community scope, Commons tier, listed and joinable by anyone, with no group key to derive a destination from. Whether a public room's destination may announce, and how it is resolved without a per-group HKDF, is stated by neither.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.1: Projection ceiling **`Cohort`** at every commons tier, no `authority` branch.
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)
note: session:{kind} placement and replication cells admit commons (audience everyone); CC 3.1.3.1 forbids the family at Global because it would publish an attendance map of a person's devices. The cell is flagged gap, so a careful reader goes to the text; the placement cell wants the ceiling.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "A node MUST admit a `withdraws` against a target row `T` when one line of this table holds. It MUST refuse any other with `federation_withdraws_not_admitted`."
side_b: CC 7.5.5: "the key named in `decided_by` withdraws the `decided` row, admitted because that row names it (the lineage-witness rule, as for the custodian)"
note: The admission table has five lines (quorum, signer, a key in subject_key_ids, hash proxy, delegate). A key named in the envelope member decided_by is none of them, so a node built from CC 2.4.1.1 refuses the decider's cancellation that CC 7.5.5 and CC 3.1.5 admit, unless decided_by is also in subject_key_ids, which no section says. The retirement model assumes the CC 7.5.5 reading.

side_a: CC 3.1.1: "A rename or policy change is a `supersedes`; closing the room is a `withdraws`."
side_b: CC 2.4: "so no single signer and no subject can retire a community, un-name a charter or retract a roster event"
note: The listing is a single-signer row of the founder or a moderate-holder; its withdrawal ends discovery. Read alone, "closing the room" says one signer closes the community, which CC 2.4 and CC 4.4.3.2.8 (dissolution by charter or by lapse of the last deciding seat) deny. The rest of the document supports CC 2.4.

side_a: CC 3.1.1: "Entity revocation (`agent` / `partner` / `license`). Immediate, non-rollbackable."
side_b: CC 2.4.1.1: "An occurrence revocation, a key grant and a cosignature already sent are never withdrawn either"
note: Still present. The never-withdrawn list omits the entity revocation, so rule 1 (condition: none) admits its attester's withdrawal while CC 3.1.1 reads non-rollbackable. The data (revocation:{entity_type}:{reason} withdraw by author) follows rule 1.

side_a: CC 3.4.13: "when a guardian withdraws their own binding (`withdraws`), their signature no longer counts toward any prior co-signed widening"
side_b: CC 2.4.1.1: "**A withdrawal reaches forward only.** Acts taken while `T` stood still stand."
note: Known, settled on reading (the widening is read as resting on a live binding). Reported because CC 3.1.3 also says an event assembled from sufficient signatures is judged on those signatures alone, and a reader of that sentence keeps the widening.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "a `moderation:*` report or action, a `hard_case:*`, a `slashing:*` verdict, a `quarantine:*` marker"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: quarantine:{state} withdraw admitted withdrawn author,subject selfAct
note: Still present in the data. The kept list now names the quarantine marker, but family_model.json quarantine:{state} lifecycle has withdraws_by {attester, subject}, retraction_class peer, and transitions.json lets author or subject withdraw: the subject of a quarantine can lift it.

side_a: CC 3.3.6: "an eviction is a `withdraws` against the `identity_occurrence` row, proposed by a live roster key and landing under [CC 3.3.6.3](#3.3.6.3)"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: identity:occurrence withdraw admitted withdrawn author,subject selfAct
note: Still present. identity:occurrence withdraw is selfAct by author or subject in transitions.json; the text lands an eviction only under the two self-roster paths, with a window.

side_a: CC 7.5.5: "The agent key, the ladder's producer, may also withdraw it under [CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) rule 1."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: retirement:{state} withdraw admitted withdrawn author selfAct
note: Still present in part. transitions.json now has a retirement withdraw with the no-frozen guard, but its roles are author only (the decided_by key is absent) and the family_model.json lifecycle cell still reads none (held shut). Also C367.

side_a: CC 3.1.2.1: "A rebuild is a `supersedes` on the earlier Contribution, and a bad build is withdrawn by the pipeline that signed it."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: provenance:build_manifest:{target} withdraw admitted withdrawn author,subject selfAct
note: Still present. provenance:build_manifest:{target} verbs are attest and withdraw; no replace or supersede transition for a rebuild. Withdraw is by author or subject, where the text names the signing pipeline only.

side_a: CC 4.5.7: "Enable/disable is **signed by the authority and revocable** (`withdraws`)."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: watchlist:{id} attest none admitted registered selfAct
note: Still present. watchlist:{id} attest role is registered and withdraw is author or subject, selfAct; the text gives enable and disable to the group's moderate or takedown authority. Also C365.

side_a: CC 3.2: "A node MUST reject a rule-2 or rule-4 `withdraws` against a live owner-binding unless it carries a `wa_adjudication_ref`"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: self:delegates_to authorize none admitted self selfAct true none
note: Still present. self:delegates_to and self:delegates_to:agent_occurrence carry authorize only: no withdraw transition, though CC 2.4.1.2.1 ends a delegation by the principal's withdraws and CC 4.4.3.4.3 by withdrawing the delegation.

side_a: CC 3.2: "An owner ends it by a `withdraws` of the acceptance."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: lineage_witness:{stage} attest none admitted founder,owner selfAct true none
note: lineage_witness:{stage} has verbs attest only (cc-table) and one transition, attest, with undo false; the CC 8.10 card shows no way back. The text lets the node's owner end witnessing by withdrawing the acceptance, after which that key's cosignatures stop counting. The lifecycle cell of the same family (code-v61) does allow attester or subject to withdraw, so the data also disagrees with itself.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "A signature row is never withdrawn: a member that has sent its signature cannot recall it"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: cosign:{state} withdraw admitted withdrawn author selfAct
note: cosign:{state} has one withdraw transition, role author, no guard on the leaf. The text admits a withdraws of a pending row by its proposer only and refuses one naming a signature row. A kernel executing the transition lets a member recall a sent cosignature. The attest guard is leaf-conditioned; the withdraw is not.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2: "The inviter withdraws a proposal with the ordinary `withdraws`."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: membership:{stage} withdraw admitted withdrawn member cosigned
note: membership:{stage} has one withdraw transition, policy cosigned, for every stage. A proposal is a single-signer row its inviter withdraws alone (rule 1); rule 0 reaches only rows carrying additional_scrubs. The lifecycle note says "check_cosigned_withdraws; resignation self" and does not carve out the proposal either.

side_a: CC 2.4: "so no single signer and no subject can retire a community, un-name a charter or retract a roster event"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: trust:{job}:{version} withdraw admitted withdrawn author,subject selfAct
note: trust:{job}:{version} withdraw is selfAct by author or subject for every job. A trust:charter row that carries a scrub set (the keyless family root, the witness quorum the cosign_rule cell names) is a cosigned row, and rule 0 lets only the quorum withdraw it. The data does not separate the cosigned charter from the single-signer confers and accepts edges.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "Each named party may withdraw ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) rule 2); only the attester recants"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: consent:community_trust withdraw admitted withdrawn author,subject selfAct
note: The text gives recants to the attester of consent:community_trust and consent:replication ("revoked via `withdraws`/`recants`") and to a trust edge ("Retracted by `withdraws`/`recants`"). The verbs cells of consent:community_trust (attest, withdraw), consent:replication:{version} and trust:{job}:{version} carry no recant, and transitions.json has no recant transition for them.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1: "A `licensure:{community_key_id}` row is a **cosigned row** ([CC 2.4](#2.4)) whose protocol source is the authority named in the dimension."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: licensure:{authority_id} attest none admitted registered selfAct
note: Still present. licensure:{authority_id} has cosign_rule none and one-signer attest and withdraw; the text admits an organisation-named licence only when its signature set meets the affiliation's protocol (CC 3.3.9 M-of-N write rule) and retracts it by the same quorum.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7: "A member votes for the Goal by cosigning it, and the row is admitted only when its full scrub set meets the group's protocol at `asserted_at`."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: goal:{scale} attest none admitted registered selfAct
note: goal:{scale}, approach:{goal_id}, method:{approach_id}:{substrate_rung} and progress_measure:{method_id} have cosign_rule none and one-signer attest, withdraw and supersede for every row. The text makes a group-declared row (authority_id naming the group) a cosigned row, and says its supersedes, withdraws and recants stand only when cosigned under the same protocol. The data has no arm for the group-declared form, so one member could declare or retire a group's Goal.

side_a: CC 4.2.1: "**Durable** settings are earned by **quorum, never by having been exercised**."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: mesh_config:{key} attest none admitted steward selfAct
note: mesh_config:{key} has cosign_rule none and a one-signer steward attest with no guard on TTL. The text lets one holder set only emergency relief (threshold 1, TTL at most 72 h, not renewable back to back) and gives a durable setting to the root's own quorum. The data does not separate the two, so one steward key could write a durable setting. (C379 is the text side of the same rule.)

side_a: CC 4.2.6: "`W` = 72 h ([CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.7)); under a declared severe-degradation state the proposal's `window_until` MAY reach 7 d"

note: The policy row that carries every accord threshold but the fire has window 0 and class none, while the text gives an accord roster change a participation window (72 h, up to 7 d) after which the tally closes. The window does exist in the data, as a clock on group:roster in reactions.json (admission_freshness_window_secs, max accord_roster_window_max_secs), but it is counted from first_held by receipt, where the text has the proposer sign `window_until` into the proposal. A reader of the policy table alone finds no window.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.3: "**It is a cosigned row by a strict majority of the standing roster** (`additional_scrubs[]`, [CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md))"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: accord:lifecycle:{kind} attest none admitted holder mirror
note: accord:lifecycle:{kind} has cosign_rule none (code-v61) though the column vocabulary has the value accord, and its policy is mirror over rows accord_halt and accord_majority. side_a: CC 4.2.6: "**`DECIMATION` is a quorum-computation rule over the existing `CONSTITUTIONAL` kind — not a new invocation verb.**"
side_b: CC 4.2.6: "A **halt** is the `accord:invoke` row and nothing else. A **roster change** rides **three** hybrid-signed (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65, JCS-canonical) objects, and none of them exists on the fire path"
note: The decimation rule is the roster-change participation window; the constitutional kind is the one-holder halt, which has no quorum to compute ("no live set, no vote"). The DECIMATION sentence is left from an earlier design where the halt was counted. The table and the wire-shape paragraph agree with each other.

side_a: CC 4.5.12.3: "A new `identity_occurrence` is admitted on a signature from EITHER the root `identity_key_id` (until the self evicts its genesis key) OR any currently active occurrence of that identity"
side_b: CC 4.5.12.3: "At two or more it is a strict majority of the live roster, the proposer included, or the lone path after its window"
note: The opening sentence states single-vouch admission for every occurrence; the same paragraph then sends a user-role key through the self-roster door of CC 3.3.6.3 and a node through its owner-binding. A reader of the first sentence alone admits a thief's new device on one stolen key. CC 3.3.6.3 and the self_roster_add policy row support the second.

side_a: CC 4.2.6: "within `halt_fuse_secs` of the halt, or the lone halt lapses"
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1: "The fuse is counted from receipt on the node's own clock, never from the signer-chosen `asserted_at`."
note: Known, settled on reading: the table phrase names no instant and the fuse paragraph is the rule. The phrase stands in both tables (CC 4.2.1.1 now reads "admitted at a node before that node's own fuse lapses"; CC 4.2.6 keeps the old wording).

side_a: CC 3.3.13: "Multi-sig signed (HumanityAccord / StewardTriple / WaQuorum / OneOfSix) per [CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md)"
side_b: CC 4.2.3: "a strict majority of the standing roster for every accord threshold, with the halt alone firing on one holder's row"
note: Known in part (C054, the citation). The four signer-set names appear nowhere else in Parts 1 to 7; CC 4.2.1 defines no StewardTriple, WaQuorum or OneOfSix, so the signing rule for accord_data cannot be built from the cell.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.6: "MUST equal a `SignedTreeHead.root_hash` actually published for `log_id = "stream:<stream_id>"` ([CC 5.3.3.3](#5.3.3.3)) at `tree_size ≥ K`. A phantom / self-invented root → REJECT."
side_b: CC 8.10: "attest: `one transparency_log:inclusion@admitted[val:root_hash=val:chunk_root] else advise` (CC 5.3.3.6)"
note: The repair of C358 and C433 removed the refusing clause altogether. The one guard left on delivery_receipt:{stream_id} is the recommended inclusion proof (step 3) and it only advises. Nothing in the data refuses a receipt whose chunk_root is no published head (step 2, a MUST with REJECT), nor one on an accountable stream whose head is not witness-cosigned. A kernel built from the card admits phantom-root receipts.

side_a: CC 3.2: "Every roster-affecting row MUST be **covered** by a new version within one cadence of its `effective_at`, and nothing else moves the head."
side_b: CC 3.2: "The founder quorum is never on a timer. The cadence duty is the **witnesses'**."
note: The first sentence puts a MUST with a deadline on the conferring quorum ("The duty is the conferring quorum's"); six lines on the same quorum is never on a timer. The three listed consequences (refuse a disagreeing version, mark the head lagging, the row takes effect anyway) are what a node does either way, so the behaviour is the same; the MUST is unenforced by design and reads as a duty the later sentence denies.

side_a: CC 2.6.5: "Certificate Transparency v2.0 (CT-bis); MUST be used for new transparency-log integrations; older 6962 instances continue to interoperate"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.7: "instantiated per-stream as separate log instances under the same RFC 6962 algorithm"
note: Every normative log statement names RFC 6962 (CC 3.1.2 inclusion and consistency proofs; CC 5.3.1.1 "base64 RFC 6962, section 2.1.2"; per-stream logs), while the references table requires RFC 9162 for new integrations. The Merkle tree hash is the same in both; the proof and tree-head encodings are not. CC 2.6.1.8 (planned) speaks of "the RFC 9162 tree".

side_a: CC 5.3.6.1: "consistency proof against the prior STH it cosigned is absent or does not verify"
side_b: CC 5.3.1.1: "missing proof when a prior STH exists or a tree_size behind the witness's prior cosigned STH → `MALFORMED_REQUEST`"
note: The error-table cell gives CONSISTENCY_PROOF_INVALID for an absent proof and, in its next sentence, MALFORMED_REQUEST for a missing one. CC 5.3.1.1 gives MALFORMED_REQUEST for missing and CONSISTENCY_PROOF_INVALID only for a proof that does not reconstruct both roots. Two implementers return different tokens for the same refusal.

side_a: CC 5.3.1.1: "The Registry MUST reject `POST /v1/transparency/sth/cosign` requests that omit the `consistency_proof_*` fields OR whose consistency proof does not verify against the named prior STH."
side_b: CC 5.3.1.1: "A witness's first cosignature is exempt ("from genesis")."
note: The MUST refuses every request that omits the fields; the next paragraph exempts a witness's first cosignature and refuses a missing proof only "when a prior STH exists". A reader of the first paragraph alone refuses a new witness's first cosignature.

side_a: CC 3.3.10.1: "Heads MUST be committed to the [CC 5.4.5](part_5_transport_substrate.md) per-community witness chain at a declared cadence; the cadence IS the equivocation-exposure window"
side_b: CC 5.4.5: "it is NOT the [CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1) **transparency-log witness** (an independent STH cosigner providing append-only / consistency / anti-equivocation guarantees)"
note: The ledger clause anchors heads against equivocation in the CC 5.4.5 chain, which CC 5.4.5 defines as a privacy discipline on what commitments reveal and forbids substituting for the anti-equivocation witness. CC 3.2 likens a founder roster's re-sync "from the witness plane" to a ledger owner's. Which witness construction detects a ledger fork is not decidable from the two sections.

side_a: CC 4.1.5: "downstream `transparency_log:inclusion` from a witness who actually retrieved it"
side_b: CC 3.1.2: "RFC 6962 inclusion proof for an audit leaf."
note: CC 4.1.5 uses the inclusion row as a retriever's attestation of reception, signed by a witness; the registry row is a Merkle inclusion proof with no emitter rule, and the data lets any registered key sign it (transitions.tsv: attest by registered). One name, two things, and the signer differs.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: "Cosignatures with `signed_at` farther than 5 minutes from the STH's published `signed_at` MUST be rejected."
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: receipt future-skew <=5 min, us resolution (check_instant_binding); no W
note: transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size} freshness is the generic cell: judged at receipt, future skew only. The text bounds a cosignature on both sides of the STH's own published signed_at, so a cosignature dated long before the head is refused by the text and admitted by the cell. (C120 covers the lineage-head route, measured against the Registry's clock.)

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.5: "g.valid_until passed without renewal"
side_b: data manifests/reactions.json: "default": "consent_temporary_ttl_secs",
note: reactions.json has two expiry entries for consent:state:{stance} leaf granted, both optional on valid_until: one with no default (cites CC 3.3.1, 4.4.3.5.5) and one with default consent_temporary_ttl_secs counted from asserted_at (cites CC 4.4.3.5.6). The text lapses only a grant that carries a valid_until; 14 days is the TEMPORARY bundle's, and constants.tsv says so ("for a temporary grant that states no `valid_until`"). The second entry has no condition naming the temporary stream, so a kernel reading it lapses every undated grant at 14 days.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: "A time-boxed guest is a widening with `valid_until`, and the seat lapses at that instant."
side_b: data manifests/reactions.json: "member": "expires_at",
note: The only expiry entry for membership:{stage} is the proposal's expires_at; the family_model lifecycle cell reads "expires_at honoured". Nothing in the data lapses a widening at its valid_until, so a time-boxed guest stays seated. The same gap holds for identity:occurrence (CC 4.4.3.4.6 drops an occurrence past valid_until from the self-collective) and for capacity_assurance:reversible_pending (CC 3.1.2: the binding MUST lapse unless resolved within its valid_until): neither has an expiry entry.

side_a: CC 2.1: "| `expires_at` | `membership:proposal`, REQUIRED |"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7: "REQUIRED on census:share:{class}:v1 and census:member:share:v1, where it is the period's end (census_return_expired after it)."
note: Still present. CC 2.1 requires expires_at on a membership proposal only; the signed-object table requires it on the two census share rows only and marks it otherwise OPTIONAL; CC 3.1.3.3 makes the 72-hour window of a custody report "the claim's `expires_at`" and reactions.json requires it there. Three lists of where the member is required.

side_a: CC 2.1: "If set, consumer policy treats the attestation as stale after that point, independent of the row's own `expires_at`."
side_b: CC 3.1.3.1: "A row without `valid_until` is malformed on this family."
note: The envelope table lists valid_until as required by nothing and as consumer-policy staleness (CC 2.6.1.7: OPTIONAL, "Consumer-policy staleness"). The session claim, the rendezvous route, config:load, emergency mesh_config and an incapacity binding each require it, and there it is a lapse every reader computes at the same instant ("never a consumer-local timeout"), with the substrate emitting consent:state:expired on it for a grant. A careful reader follows the family home; the envelope row understates the member.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "the delegate holds a live `delegates_to` from them, and the kept list binds the delegate as it binds them"
side_b: CC 3.2: "A recovery authority `R` holding `delegates_to(K → R, scope: [owner_binding_recovery])` may sign under rule 4."
note: Rule 3 names the scope its proxy must hold (consent_revocation); rule 4 names none, so read alone it lets a delegate under any scope (a moderate or act-on-behalf edge) withdraw its principal's rows. CC 3.2 applies rule 4 with a scope that names the act, and CC 4.5.5 says an absent field admits nothing and a delegate's scope is never widened. The rest of the document supports a scope condition; the table does not state one.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "**Substrate-emitted, not subject-emitted** — it records an observed clock event, not a stance"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: consent:state:{stance} attest none admitted owner,self selfAct
note: The one attest transition of consent:state:{stance} has roles owner and self for every leaf. The expired leaf is emitted by the substrate (reactions.json names identity:substrate_persist as the emitter), so the transition's role list refuses the row the reaction must emit, and admits a subject-signed expired row the text reserves to the substrate.
